records.title: High-altitude decompression illness: case report and discussion

exposure_details.peak_revision_basis: The earlier value describes typical training. The actual peak printed for the three cases is 26,000 ft.
exposure_details.symptom_onset_phase_all_three: during the first commercial flight after training
exposure_details.scope: The case series supplies no matching denominator for the later flight. The course count is not reused as a risk set.

table_1_cases.pain_sites: Began in the knees and spread to hips, lower back, shoulders, elbows and neck.
table_1_cases.exam_findings: Pain and tenderness with movement prevented walking. Fluid was visible behind the left tympanic membrane.
table_1_cases.possible_oxygen_toxicity_during_hbot: Right thigh fasciculation after 30 minutes of treatment.
table_1_cases.followup: Burning on respiration on days 2–9 after treatment. The authors describe it as typical of pulmonary oxygen toxicity.

table_1_cases.other_symptoms: Left arm numbness and difficulty breathing.
table_1_cases.exam_findings: Anxious. Reduced left arm pinprick sensation from wrist to shoulder compared with the right.
table_1_cases.possible_oxygen_toxicity_during_hbot: Dizziness and malaise at 70 and 200 minutes after treatment started.
table_1_cases.followup: The authors report no further problems. Follow-up duration is unspecified.

table_1_cases.pain_sites: Retrosternal and left pectoral chest pain, headache and mid-to-upper back pain.
table_1_cases.other_symptoms: Difficulty swallowing and speaking for 20 minutes, irritability, shortness of breath, and tingling in both calves.
table_1_cases.exam_findings: Nystagmus and slight erythema of the left tympanic membrane.
table_1_cases.followup: The authors report no further problems. Follow-up duration is unspecified.

hbot_course.note: Table 1 footnote gives total treatment duration. The patient-level resolution times use time from treatment start. The report describes about 9.5 hours of symptoms before treatment, without exact patient-level timings.

protocols.note: The paper points to the cadet hypoxia and decompression tests for profile parameters.

records.note: The report does not identify a Czech DCS numerator, at-risk count or observation window. The rate concerns broad dysbarism. The paper mentions more than 120 hyperbaric oxygen patients per year for all indications. That treatment volume does not define a hypobaric exposure denominator.

observations.locator: Printed p. 19-1, paragraph before Hypobaric Chambers
observations.note: Common symptoms include ear or sinus pain, nosebleed and abdominal pain. The passage concerns assessment before hypo- and hyperbaric exposures. The size, time period and composition of the population behind 10% are unspecified.
